title: GOAT-Bench: Safety Insights to Large Multimodal Models through Meme-Based Social Abuse
measurement_description: The paper measured the ability of Large Multimodal Models to detect hateful memes targeting people based on their religion, as part of a broader benchmark on social abuse. It also analyzed model bias where content involving specific religious groups (e.g., Muslims) was more likely to be incorrectly flagged as hateful.
findings: The study found that Large Multimodal Models struggle with implicit hateful content that can involve religion (e.g., a meme referencing Adolf Hitler and 'gas'). Furthermore, a case study on GPT-4V revealed a potential bias where the model incorrectly flagged a non-hateful meme as hateful, with the paper suggesting this misclassification was due to the model's oversensitivity to content involving Muslim communities.
